biography.plain_text: Max Näder was a German entrepreneur who rebuilt and expanded Ottobock, the prosthetics business founded by his father-in-law, Otto Bock. Working with his wife, Maria, he established its post-war base in Duderstadt and developed it into an international medical technology group. He handed management to their son, Hans Georg, in 1990.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Ottobock, Max Näder helped turn prosthetic limbs into systems whose parts could be adjusted and replaced. His modular leg design used a pyramid connector to join the foot, knee and socket, allowing technicians to change alignment and exchange components. He also brought muscle-controlled arm prostheses to market, widening the range of objects their users could grasp.

He had trained in both orthopaedic mechanics and commerce before leading the business, combining practical product development with an understanding of customers. Through the independent Otto Bock Foundation, which he established in 1987, he encouraged doctors, therapists and orthopaedic technicians to work together.
